note: Flat faces of the Met gui (KIT.md § Flat faces). The vessel is ROUND: each face is the plane seen down the photograph's own line of sight (normal tilted 4° up, the camera's elevation fitted from the rim and foot ellipses, dossier §b.1), so the flattened photo is the photograph's orthographic projection, and the model is rendered down the same normal: both show the curved wall foreshortened identically. Points are landmarks on the rim, foot and centre line with their true 3D positions; perspective (camera ≈ 2 m) is the residual. Trust the centre third most (|x| < 50 mm); beyond |x| ≈ 65 mm the wall turns away (foreshortening > 2:1).

DP218261.note: face A head-on, camera ≈ 4° above the rim centre

face-front.label: face A, whole vessel rim to ground (chord view down the camera axis)

face-front.fit: least-squares fit of the points: rms 0.86 mm, max 1.4 mm (tools/faces.mjs --rectify prints it)

face-mask.label: face A, main mask register (y 41–86)

face-mask.fit: least-squares fit of the points: rms 0.86 mm, max 1.4 mm (tools/faces.mjs --rectify prints it)

face-neck.label: face A, rising blades + dragon frieze with the frontal head (y 85–112)

face-foot.label: face A, foot frieze and base ring (y 0–38)
